items.name: interlace-base
items.title: Interlace Base
items.description: @interlace/ui — the additive CSS baseline every component needs: motion tokens, type scale, container widths, the xs breakpoint, radius derived from --radius, a named z-index layer scale, layered brand + semantic colour tokens in OKLCH, and a color-scheme that follows the dark class so native controls match. Changes nothing the host app already styles.

items.name: theme
items.title: Interlace Theme
items.description: @interlace/ui — the Interlace look as shadcn cssVars: points your --primary, --background, --radius and the rest at Interlace's burnt-orange brand tokens (light + dark, AAA). Opt-in; components work without it.

items.name: interlace-foundation
items.title: Interlace Foundation
items.description: @interlace/ui — opt-in page-level styling: Inter and JetBrains Mono on font-sans / font-mono, the preflight (body colours, WCAG 2.2 focus ring, media reset, scrollbars), and the fumadocs colour bridge. Restyles the host app by design.

items.name: a11y-starter
items.title: A11y Starter
items.description: @interlace/ui — the three a11y primitives + the reduced-motion hook every consumer should install on day one.

items.name: layout-starter
items.title: Layout Starter
items.description: @interlace/ui — the six layout primitives that compose every page. One install, the LAYOUT_PHILOSOPHY contract is satisfied.

items.name: mdx-starter
items.title: MDX Starter
items.description: @interlace/ui — the components most MDX pipelines need (Callout, Prose, CodeBlock, Tag), wired through a default mdx-components.tsx.

items.name: cn
items.title: cn — class-name merge utility
items.description: @interlace/ui — the cn() helper, alias-compatible with shadcn. Merges Tailwind class lists deterministically.

items.name: use-reduced-motion
items.title: useReducedMotion hook
items.description: @interlace/ui — the `useReducedMotion` hook every interactive primitive uses to gate animations on the user's OS preference.

items.name: motion-token
items.title: Motion token reader
items.description: @interlace/ui — reads the `--ease-*` and `--duration-*` tokens from an element, so animations started from script retune with the brand like the CSS does.

items.name: theme-tokens
items.title: Theme token manifest
items.description: @interlace/ui — the registry of themes and the list of every `--interlace-*` token a theme must define. A missing token does not throw; it silently inherits the previous theme's value.

items.name: use-theme
items.title: useTheme hook
items.description: @interlace/ui — reads and writes the theme (`data-theme`) and colour scheme (`.dark`) axes, persists to localStorage, and follows the OS when no preference is stored.

items.name: use-reading-prefs
items.title: useReadingPrefs hook
items.description: @interlace/ui — reads and writes the reader's text size (`data-text-size`) and contrast (`data-contrast`) on <html>, persists both, and follows `prefers-contrast` when no choice is stored.

items.name: intent
items.title: User intent hooks and provider
items.description: @interlace/ui — typed, vendor-neutral user intent: activate, view, dwell, commit, disclosure and form hooks, `data-intent` for server components, rage clicks and page view/leave, all reported through one `IntentProvider` adapter. Sends nothing that identifies a person.

items.name: error-report-model
items.title: Error report rules
items.description: @interlace/ui — the pure rules of error reporting: a typed report, a flood counted not repeated, a redaction hook, restore from untrusted storage, text for a diagnostics screen. No DOM, no network, no storage library.

items.name: error-report
items.title: reportError
items.description: @interlace/ui — `reportError(error, where)`, one function every caught failure goes through, with a pluggable reporter, a device-only crash log and global handlers. Sends nothing unless you set a reporter.

items.name: use-recent-errors
items.title: useRecentErrors hook
items.description: @interlace/ui — the reports kept so far, as a list that re-renders when one arrives, for a diagnostics screen.

items.name: theme-script
items.title: No-flash theme bootstrap script
items.description: @interlace/ui — the inline `<head>` script that applies the stored theme before first paint. Without it every page load flashes the default theme.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: A disclosure stack: a column of headers whose panels open and close. Wraps @base-ui/react/accordion — Base UI owns the open state (single or multiple), the keyboard model and every piece of the accordion ARIA.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: A bordered in-page message with `role="alert"`, an optional leading icon, a title and a description, in two tones (default and destructive).

items.name: aspect-ratio

items.title: Avatar

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small pill for a status, a count, a label or a tag. Renders a `<span>` by default, or whatever Base UI's `render` prop is given, so the same badge can be an anchor without losing its shape.

items.title: Button

items.description: "How are you arriving?" Pick the face that fits. Everyone answers in one tap, in the lobby while the room fills or at the start of a session, and the room's mood shows as a spread: how many chose each, the one most chose, and, when the same question was…

items.name: closer-game
items.title: Closer Game
items.description: Guess a number by sliding to it. The player sets a value on a slider (or types it), locks it in, and the answer slides out from their guess to where it really is, with the gap between them shaded and said in words: "900 off. Close." Scoring lives in…

items.name: daily-puzzle
items.title: Daily Puzzle
items.description: The frame around a daily game: its name, today's number and date, how far through the rounds the player is, and, once they finish, a countdown to the next one. The game itself is the children, so any round (a CloserGame, a GuessReveal, your own) sits…

items.name: debate-corners
items.title: Debate Corners
items.description: Pick a corner, then defend it. A statement with two to four positions, one for each corner of the room: each person stands in the corner they pick, can move until the host locks the corners, and the host calls one corner at a time to defend its position.…

items.name: dot-vote
items.title: Dot Vote
items.description: After a brainstorm, the room chooses: each person spreads a few dots across the ideas (two on one idea means "this one, really"), sends them, and watches the ideas rank themselves as everyone's dots come in. It pairs with `TextWall` or `QuestionBoard` for…

items.name: duel
items.title: Duel
items.description: Two players, one game, by link. The first player finishes and sends a challenge (`DuelInvite`); the second opens it and sees who they are up against (`DuelCard`); after playing the same game, both see the rounds side by side (`DuelCompare`). The challenge…

items.name: exit-ticket
items.title: Exit Ticket
items.description: Three quick questions as people leave, while it is fresh: how likely to recommend (0 to 10, grouped the standard way into promoters, passives and detractors), a rating on a short scale, and a choice. Answers go in with one button and can be changed until…

items.name: goal-ring
items.title: Goal Ring
items.description: How far today is toward a daily goal: a ring that fills as points come in, the count in its middle, and a check once the goal is met. It is a `meter`, so assistive tech reads "15 of 20 XP" without the ring.

items.name: groups
items.title: Groups
items.description: Pairs, small groups and teams. `GroupCard` is what one person's phone shows: which group they are in, who they are with, what to talk about and for how long. `GroupGrid` is the shared screen: every group with its people, where a reshuffle glides each name…

items.name: join-code
items.title: Join Code
items.description: How people get into a live room: the address to visit, a code to type there, and a QR code that does both in one scan. Built for the host's big screen first (`size="stage"`), and just as usable on a phone that wants to pass the room on, with a copy-link…

items.name: leaderboard
items.title: Leaderboard
items.description: A group's board for a game: rank, name and score, ties sharing a rank, the viewing player's row marked (and kept even when it falls below the top rows), and the whole board held back until enough people have played that no one's score stands alone. Ranking…

items.name: level-meter
items.title: Level Meter
items.description: A player's level and how far they are into the next: the level, a bar of XP, the XP still to go, and, right after a round, the XP just earned. The arithmetic is `levelFor` / `gainXp` in `progress-model.ts`, exported so a server shows the same level.

items.name: live-room
items.title: Live Room
items.description: A game night on one big screen and everyone's phones. The host opens a room and shows its JoinCode; players scan or type it and land in the lobby; the host starts, everyone sees the same countdown, plays the same rounds, and the night ends on a Podium. The…

items.name: milestones
items.title: Milestones
items.description: The marks along a path a player is on (a 3, 7 and 30-day streak; levels 5, 10 and 20): the ones reached, the next one with how far is left, and a few beyond. It shows where the player is going, not a wall of locked trophies, so only a window around the…

items.name: note-board
items.title: Note Board
items.description: A shared board of sticky notes in columns: a retrospective ("Keep / Change / Try"), an affinity sort, a "before / during / after" map. People post a note into a column, and the room sorts them by moving notes between columns. Every screen folds the same…

items.name: order-game
items.title: Order Game
items.description: Put a handful of items in order: events from earliest to latest, places from smallest to largest. The player drags rows by their handle, or moves them with the arrow keys or the up and down buttons, then locks in. The rows then glide into the right order…

items.name: pair-talk
items.title: Pair Talk
items.description: Pair talk for a live room: the host pairs everyone (a group of three when the room is odd), each pair gets a prompt card and a timer, and "swap partners" pairs everyone again with someone new. Each phone shows who its partner is, the card and the time…

items.name: picture-reveal
items.title: Picture Reveal
items.description: A picture under tiles that come away a few at a time while the room guesses. The presenter moves `step`; every screen uncovers the same tiles in the same seeded order, spread across the picture. Phones guess with `TypeAnswer` (or `QuizQuestion`), and…

items.name: pin-drop
items.title: Pin Drop
items.description: A pin on a picture (a map, a floor plan, a diagram). On a phone, `PinDrop` lets each person place one pin by tap, drag or arrow keys. With an `answer` it is "Where is it?": once the host reveals, the answer appears, a line joins it to the viewer's pin, and…

items.name: podium
items.title: Podium
items.description: The end of a game: the top three on steps, second and third rising first and the winner last, with a burst for first place. Below it, everyone else, so no one has to wonder where they came. Ranking is the leaderboard's (`rankEntries`), so ties share a…

items.name: points-split
items.title: Points Split
items.description: Spend a budget of points across options. `PointsSplit` is a phone: each option has a minus and a plus, a bar shows how much of the budget sits on it, and a counter says what is left; Send unlocks when the budget is spent. `PointsTotals` is the screen: the…

items.name: poll
items.title: Poll
items.description: One question, one tap. The options are plain buttons; tapping one casts the vote, and the options turn into the results in place, with the bars growing to everyone's shares and the viewer's choice named. There is no submit step, because a poll that asks…

items.name: prediction
items.title: Prediction
items.description: "Who will win?" on a phone: the room calls an outcome before it happens, locks it in, and waits. Nobody sees how the room called it until the host settles it, so a call is the person's own read. Then the room's spread appears with the outcome marked, and…

items.name: qr-code
items.title: Qr Code
items.description: A QR code for a link or a short text, drawn as one SVG path from the pure encoder in `qr-model.ts`. No dependency, no canvas, no image request: it renders on the server and stays sharp at any size, from a phone card to a projector.

items.name: quadrant
items.title: Quadrant
items.description: A 2 x 2 grid: two questions at once ("how hard / how important"). Each person places one dot on a square pad, by tapping, dragging or the arrow keys, then sees the room on the same grid: where the dots crowd, how many sit in each quarter, the room's…

items.name: question-board
items.title: Question Board
items.description: Questions from the room, ranked by the room. People ask from their phone (`QuestionAsk`), vote up the questions they want answered (`QuestionBoard`), and a moderator approves, pins, answers or hides them (`QuestionQueue`) before anything typed reaches a…

items.name: quiz-question
items.title: Quiz Question
items.description: A multiple-choice question with the energy of a live quiz and the manners of a form: big answer tiles you can tap, click or pick with a number key, an optional clock that rewards speed, and a reveal that marks the right answer, says in words how you did…

items.name: ranking
items.title: Ranking
items.description: A room ranks the same items by preference. `RankChoices` is a phone: the items in a seeded starting order (so nobody's first item is favoured by where it was printed), moved with up and down buttons or the arrow keys on each row's handle, then sent.…

items.name: rating
items.title: Rating
items.description: A scale question for a room: how familiar, how likely to recommend, how are you feeling. Each person picks one step and sends it; then they see the room's answers on the same scale, their own step marked, the room's average, and, when the question was…

items.name: reactions
items.title: Reactions
items.description: The room's pulse while someone talks. Phones tap a reaction (`ReactionBar`) and the shared screen lets it float up (`ReactionStream`); someone who wants to speak raises a hand (`RaiseHand`) and the host calls on people in the order they asked (`HandQueue`).

items.name: recall-card
items.title: Recall Card
items.description: A prompt the player answers in their head, then checks: they think of their answer, reveal the real one, and say honestly how they did. No typing and no multiple choice, so it fits anything with an answer longer than a word: a definition, a reply to a…

items.name: reflection-card
items.title: Reflection Card
items.description: A quiet minute in a loud room: one prompt ("What surprised you today?"), a field, and a promise that the answer is yours. It is private by default; when the session allows it, the writer can choose to share it with the room without their name, and only…

items.name: reminder-offer
items.title: Reminder Offer
items.description: A quiet offer of a daily nudge that the player keeps in their own calendar: pick a time, add it, done. It downloads an .ics file with one event that repeats daily (`reminder-model.ts`), so nothing is sent, no address is asked for, and the player removes it…

items.name: room-clock
items.title: Room Clock
items.description: A countdown to a host timestamp, in minutes and seconds ("7:42"), for the timers that run for minutes: a breakout, a round of pair talk. (`TimerRing` counts the seconds of a quiz round; a ring that says 600 is a poor way to say ten minutes.) The deadline…

items.name: room-goal
items.title: Room Goal
items.description: One meter for the whole room: a shared target, named milestones on the way ("Bonus round", "Group photo"), and, when given, how many rounds in a row most of the room got right. Built for the shared screen; it reads the same on a phone.

items.name: round-summary
items.title: Round Summary
items.description: The moment a round ends: what the player earned, where today's goal stands, the streak it kept, and anything new they reached (a milestone, a level). Then the next step, which the app passes as children: share, play on, come back tomorrow. It celebrates…

items.name: share-card
items.title: Share Card
items.description: How the player did today, ready to share without spoiling it: one mark per round (a band, never the answer), the score and the streak, with a Share button that opens the device's share sheet and a Copy button that puts the same text on the clipboard. The…

items.name: sound-cue-toggle
items.title: Sound Cue Toggle
items.description: The switch for a room's sound cues, and the words for them. Sound is off until a person turns it on (a browser keeps a page silent until a tap, and a hall should not start making noise on its own). Every cue that plays is also written as a plain phrase…

items.name: spectrum
items.title: Spectrum
items.description: Where do you stand? A statement, two poles, and a line between them. Each person places one dot, then sees the whole room spread along the same line, their own bin marked, the room's middle drawn, and, when the statement was asked before, where the middle…

items.name: standings
items.title: Standings
items.description: The board between rounds of a live game: who is where now, and how they got there. Each player's points from this round pop up beside their name, their total counts up from where it was, and then the rows glide to their new places, with the places gained…

items.name: streak
items.title: Streak
items.description: A player's run of days: the count, a line on where today stands, and a strip of recent days, each marked played, rested, missed or still open. Rest days come from a `RestRule` (weekdays and dates that never break a run), so a habit does not punish a day…

items.name: tally-bars
items.title: Tally Bars
items.description: How everyone answered, as one bar per option with its whole percent: the results of a poll, or the spread of answers after a quiz question. The viewer's own choice is named in words, and a quiz can mark the right option, so nothing depends on colour alone.

items.name: team-board
items.title: Team Board
items.description: Team mode for a live room. The host sets up teams, balances them (or moves a player by hand), and everyone sees whose team they are on and how the teams score. The rules are `games/team-model`; the teams ride in the room (`RoomState.shared`), so a phone…

items.name: text-wall
items.title: Text Wall
items.description: The room's short answers on a shared screen: "what would you ask someone your age who lives there?". New posts rise in at the top; the presenter can put one in the spotlight, large, above the rest. Phones send with `QuestionAsk` (relabelled: "Your answer"…

items.name: timer-ring
items.title: Timer Ring
items.description: A countdown drawn as a ring that empties, with the seconds left in the middle. It counts to a deadline (a timestamp), not from a start, so a page that reloads, or several players in one room, all see the same clock.

items.name: type-answer
items.title: Type Answer
items.description: A quiz round where people type the answer. Harder than picking, and fairer than it looks: case, accents, punctuation and a slip of a letter in a long word are forgiven, while a different number never is (see `typed-answer-model`). The reveal marks the…

items.name: word-cloud
items.title: Word Cloud
items.description: The room's words, live. Phones send a word or two with `WordEntry`; the shared screen shows them as a `WordCloud` in which the words the room repeats grow, the biggest sit in the middle, and every change moves into place rather than jumping there. Anyone…

items.name: article-template
items.title: Article Template
items.description: Full-page surface for long-form articles. Composes the header (title + AuthorByline), the body (Prose-wrapped MDX/HTML), the related-posts grid, prev/next navigation, and share buttons — each in its own `<SectionBoundary>` so the page streams section-by-…

items.name: auth-template
items.title: Auth Template
items.description: Full-page surface for sign-in / sign-up / password-reset / verify-email flows. Centred narrow column with brand mark at top, form in the middle, helper link at the bottom ("Already have an account?" / "Forgot password?").

items.name: author-template
items.title: Author Template
items.description: Author profile page — bio header + their articles grid. Used by `/authors/[slug]` routes on a blog. The bio header is a multi-part card (avatar + name + role + bio + social links); the grid uses ArticleListGrid for the article list.

items.name: blog-home-template
items.title: Blog Home Template
items.description: Blog index surface. Topbar + hero (greeting / about) + ArticleListGrid (featured + recent) + optional NewsletterForm + Footer. The shape every personal / company blog reaches for.

items.name: dashboard-template
items.title: Dashboard Template
items.description: Application dashboard surface. Topbar at top, persistent left sidebar (nav links), main content area (children). The standard "logged-in app" layout: every SaaS dashboard reaches for this shape.

items.name: docs-page-template
items.title: Docs Page Template
items.description: Documentation page surface. Topbar at top, optional sidebar nav on the left (md+), main content in the centre with a `<Prose>` wrapper, and an optional TOC rail on the right (xl+).

items.name: error-template
items.title: Error Template
items.description: Full-page error surface — 404 / 500 / 503 / generic. Centred column with the status code + title + description + action buttons (back home, contact support, retry).

items.name: landing-template
items.title: Landing Template
items.description: Marketing landing page surface. Composes Topbar + Hero + (optional) FeatureGrid + (optional) TestimonialGrid + (optional) PricingTable + (optional) FAQ + CTASection + Footer — each in its own SectionBoundary so the page streams section-by-section.

items.name: registry-item-template
items.title: Registry Item Template
items.description: Full-page surface for a single registry item's documentation (`/c/[name]` on ds.interlace.tools). Composes the header (item name + description + install snippet), the anatomy diagram, the variants matrix, related-components grid, and a CTA back to the…

items.name: scorecard-template
items.title: Scorecard Template
items.description: Graded-evaluation page. Topbar + overall-grade header + per-dimension scorecard rows + optional methodology footnote + Footer.

items.name: settings-template
items.title: Settings Template
items.description: Account / app settings surface. Topbar + left tab-rail (sections) + main content area (rendered section). Server-friendly; the active section is driven by the consumer's routing (each section is a route).

items.name: stats-template
items.title: Stats Template
items.description: Public-facing metrics page. Topbar + header (title + lead) + SectionBoundary(StatGroup) + SectionBoundary(arbitrary chart/table content) + optional methodology footnote + Footer.

items.name: tag-template
items.title: Tag Template
items.description: Tag-filtered article index. Used by `/tags/[slug]` routes on a blog to show "all articles tagged #typescript" etc. Shows a header ("Tagged: #typescript") then an ArticleListGrid of matching posts.
